Chlorella sp. HS2 × ALE — Comparative Genomics

Genotype–Phenotype Working Summary & Full Pipeline

What in the genome could explain ALE's phenotype — evaluated at the strength of evidence currently behind each claim — plus the complete analytical pipeline and a point-by-point response to expert review, for independent evaluation.

Working hypothesis

ALE's tolerance shift is most plausibly explained not by large-scale genome restructuring — the two genomes are substantially collinear once duplicate content is corrected for — but by a small number of point mutations, now identified through a systematic, artifact-filtered, genome-wide screen rather than a hand-picked shortlist. The headline finding is EPHA: absent in ALE as of April 2023, present at 98% allele frequency by October 2024 — arising and fixing during the continuous passaging, independently re-discovered by an unbiased genome-wide funnel with no prior knowledge of which sites had been proposed before. A second strong candidate, CLPB3 (a stress-response chaperone), shows textbook standing-variation selection: HS2 stably heterozygous across three independent collection dates, ALE rising from 4% to 83% over the same window. One originally-proposed candidate (PEL1/SLAD) has been retracted after full re-validation showed it to be HS2's own background heterozygosity, never ALE-specific — reported here because retracting a wrong claim under closer scrutiny is itself part of the evidence this analysis is trustworthy.

01

Genome architecture: conserved, not rearranged

Both strains were assembled independently from HiFi long reads and corrected for retained haplotig/duplicate content using cutoffs anchored to each assembly's own validated single-copy coverage (HS2: 158×, ALE: 204×) — automatic cutoff detection had misfired badly on first pass (locked onto a spurious 16× peak) and was discarded in favor of manual cutoffs tied to hifiasm's own validated coverage.

Cross-genome alignment on the corrected assemblies shows a largely collinear relationship — 184 alignment blocks between HS2 and ALE, no gross rearrangement, consistent with a direct descendant under selection rather than a divergent strain. Self-alignment of each genome against itself, before correction, had turned up multiple near-100.0%-identity duplicate blocks tens of kilobases long — too perfect to be ordinary heterozygosity. That duplicate content is exactly what purge_dups removed: completeness is unchanged before/after purging (proof the correction didn't eat real gene content), while duplication collapsed sharply. Smudgeplot (FastK → hetmers → manual peak classification, after four internal tool bugs were bypassed) independently confirms the residual signal is genuine AB heterozygosity, not a masked duplication bump — the direct, purpose-built test the earlier draft of this section was missing.

03

Candidate genotypic changes

Re-derived from a systematic, five-criterion genome-wide screen (§5) rather than a hand-picked shortlist — the three originally-proposed candidates were re-examined under the same rigor as everything else, with one retraction, one recharacterization, and one confirmation, plus new candidates the unbiased screen surfaced independently.

PEL1 / SLADptg000019l:1,297,950 · C→T · SNPretracted

Originally proposed as ALE-specific. Full re-validation — two independent callers, both reference directions, five independent short-read samples across three collection dates (April 2023, November 2023, October 2024) — shows this is HS2's own background heterozygosity, present identically in HS2 whether mapped onto its own or ALE's assembly, and entirely absent from every ALE short-read sample. Never ALE-specific. Retracted rather than quietly dropped.

2 callers agree: HS2-only0% short-read alt-allele support in ALE, all 5 samples
ODP25 / EPHAptg000051l:296,388 · C→A · SNPconfirmed — headline candidate

Confirmed by both callers, both reference directions, and independently re-discovered by the unbiased genome-wide funnel with no prior knowledge this locus had been proposed before — one of only 30 candidates genome-wide to pass every criterion. Short-read data adds a clean temporal signature: undetectable in ALE as of April 2023 (0%, matching HS2's 0% at every timepoint), then 98% allele frequency by October 2024. This mutation arose and fixed during the continuous passaging, not before it.

GATK + bcftools agree, both directions0%→98% allele frequency, Apr 2023→Oct 2024quality-verified transcript, 99.1% cov / 100% idy
SYGM2 / GLOXptg000082l:318,835 · 34bp→32bp · INDELrecharacterized — needs targeted confirmation

Confirmed by both callers and both reference directions as a standing-variation shift (HS2 heterozygous → ALE homozygous), not a novel mutation — caught specifically because this project's genotype-aware comparison method (as opposed to naive presence/absence subtraction) is sensitive to zygosity shifts. Sits in a CA-repeat microsatellite, the same category responsible for 87% of artifacts filtered out of the genome-wide candidate pool (§5) — it does not clear the unconditional repeat-artifact filter on its own, but carries independent multi-axis long-read support and a real gene match (GLOX, aldehyde oxidase) that the filtered-out artifacts lack. Recommend targeted orthogonal confirmation (e.g. PCR fragment-length assay spanning the repeat) rather than either dropping it or reporting it at the same confidence as the unconditionally-passing candidates.

GO:0004031 aldehyde oxidase activityconfirmed by 2 callers, both directionssits in a microsatellite — needs PCR confirmation
CLPB3ptg000007l:1,269,122 · A→C · shiftednew — strongest mechanistic case

Surfaced by the unbiased genome-wide screen, not part of the original hypothesis-driven shortlist. The cleanest temporally-resolved case in the entire dataset: HS2 sits stably at 33–36% allele frequency across three independent collection dates spanning 18 months — that three-timepoint stability is itself strong evidence of real background variation, not noise — while ALE rises from 4% (Apr 2023) to 83% (Oct 2024), tracking the same window EPHA newly emerged in. Clp chaperone/protease family, directly stress-response-related.

3-timepoint HS2 stability (33–36%)4%→83% ALE rise, Apr 2023→Oct 2024Clp chaperone/protease — stress response
ACOX4ptg000006l:711,536 · C→A · ale_onlynew

Acyl-CoA oxidase — lipid metabolism. Already at high frequency in the earliest available ALE short-read sample (April 2023), suggesting this change arose earlier than the sampling window or fixed unusually fast. Thematically consistent with this strain's independently published carbon-reallocation-to-lipid halotolerance mechanism (Yun et al.).

lipid metabolismalready fixed by earliest sampled timepoint

Full candidate table — 30 unconditionally-passing candidates plus 146 with partial evidence, per-timepoint allele frequencies, and temporal-pattern classification (6 categories) — in the supplementary variant table.

The 9 sure candidates with a confident locus-level gene annotation, grouped by the annotated molecular function of their UniProt BLASTX best-hit into four thematic areas plausibly relevant to hydrolysate stress tolerance (xenobiotic/epoxide detoxification; peroxisomal β-oxidation → glyoxylate carbon flux; proteostasis / chaperone–ubiquitin-proteasome; cell-wall remodeling). Presented as hypothesis-generating: every functional label is a cross-species homology best-hit (spanning M. tuberculosis to human to Arabidopsis), not an experimentally characterized Chlorella function, and the grouping is our own thematic organization rather than a statistically tested pathway enrichment.

04

Cross-validation — the five-criterion funnel

Rather than validating only the three originally-proposed candidates, we applied a pre-specified, five-criterion filter to the full pool of 4,146 genome-wide ALE-associated sites: (1) concordant between bcftools and GATK, (2) confirmed in the reciprocal (ALE-as-reference) direction, (3) short-read supported, (4) clear of self-synteny duplicated regions, (5) not a homopolymer/microsatellite repeat-slippage artifact.

Criterion 5 required a real methodological correction mid-analysis

Criteria 1–4 alone identified 1,357 candidates — but manual inspection showed the large majority were homopolymer/short-tandem-repeat length changes, the well-documented signature of polymerase-slippage miscalling. A systematic repeat-unit detector (period 1–6bp) showed 87.0% of these 1,357 candidates were repeat-region artifacts that happened to pass all four other criteria simply because the artifact is reproducible across callers, directions, and platforms — i.e. criteria 1–4 alone are insufficient to exclude this class. After exclusion: 176 candidates pass the core funnel; 30 also have direct short-read support.

Gene-level annotation was itself quality-gated, not taken at face value from raw GMAP output: transcript alignments required ≥90% coverage, ≥90% identity, and ≤50kb span (excluding chimeric/mis-extended alignments — 142 of 78,759 raw alignments failed this and were dropped). Gene names were matched at the Trinity locus level, not exact isoform ID, since functional annotation was not exhaustively run per isoform; every gene call is tagged isoform-exact, locus-level, or no-hit so it stays individually traceable to source records.

05

Comparison across HS2-lineage strains

HS2 sits at the center as the shared ancestor for three independently-selected derivatives: ALE (full lignocellulosic hydrolysate: salinity + furanic compounds, PacBio HiFi, this study's primary focus), HS19 (NaOCl / oxidative-chlorine stress, Illumina short-read), and HMF (5-hydroxymethylfurfural alone — the furanic sub-component of ALE's full selection — Illumina short-read, two independent timepoints).

An asymmetry that must be stated plainly

HS19 and HMF variant calls have not been through the same five-criterion funnel as ALE (single caller, single baseline subtraction, no repeat-artifact filter). Extrapolating ALE's ~4% post-funnel survival rate, HS19/HMF's raw private-variant counts (2,290 and 3,387) plausibly correspond to only ~90–140 real candidates each — not the raw totals. The gene-symbol overlap with ALE (17 genes with HS19, 24 with HMF) is suggestive, not confirmed; a defensible convergent-evolution claim requires applying the identical funnel to HS19/HMF, flagged here as specific follow-up work rather than asserted.

What is defensible now: three exact-position matches, independent of the gene-symbol/annotation asymmetry above because they compare raw called positions directly — SCP46 (ptg000019l:859,524, ALE–HMF exact match), and two unnamed positions (ptg000005l:299,006 with HS19; ptg000012l:2,850,217 with HMF). That HMF and ALE's clearest overlap includes a locus under a selection condition that is a mechanistic subset of ALE's full exposure is the most mechanistically coherent convergence signal in the dataset — reported as worth targeted follow-up, not confirmed.

06

Full analytical pipeline

Complete, command-level detail for independent reproduction and evaluation. Tool versions and exact parameters are given at each stage; rationale is given wherever a non-default choice was made.

Sequencing

PacBio Revio HiFi. HS2: 23.95 Gb raw, 1,374,677 reads, N50 19,686 bp, Q20 96.26%, Q30 91.04%, GC 56.25%. ALE: 28.59 Gb raw, 1,714,417 reads, N50 18,680 bp, Q20 96.47%, Q30 91.51%, GC 56.94%.

Organelle depletion

Chloroplast + mitochondrion reference (C. sorokiniana SLA-04-derived). minimap2 -ax map-hifi against the organelle reference; organelle-mapping read IDs removed with seqkit grep -v before assembly. This step also resolved a reproducible hifiasm segfault traced to pathologically high organelle k-mer frequency.

Assembly

hifiasm 0.25.0, default parameters except -f0 (bloom-filter override, appropriate for this genome's small size — the default is calibrated for human-scale genomes). Nuclear, organelle-depleted reads: 11.14 Gb (HS2), 11.59 Gb (ALE).

Coverage validation

Single-copy read coverage independently cross-validated two ways: hifiasm's internal ha_pt_gen/purge_dups pass (homozygous coverage threshold HS2 = 157–158×, ALE = 204×) and the raw total-bases ÷ coverage k-mer estimate. Agreement between the two anchors every downstream coverage-dependent parameter below.

Assembly QC

QUAST: HS2 66.6 Mb (N50 947,597, L50 18), ALE 64.5 Mb (N50 1,329,927, L50 16). BUSCO chlorophyta_odb10: HS2 98.9% complete (S:83.9% D:14.9%), ALE 99.1% complete (S:88.9% D:10.1%).

Haplotig purging

purge_dups, manual cutoffs (-l/-m/-u) anchored to validated single-copy coverage using the tool's documented ratio (≈0.25× / 1.0× / 2.7×): HS2 -l 40 -m 158 -u 427; ALE -l 51 -m 204 -u 551. Automatic cutoff detection (calcuts unsupervised) was tested first and rejected — it locked onto a spurious 16× peak instead of true single-copy coverage, producing an unusable, catastrophically over-purged result. Result: HS2 66.6→51.26 Mb (327→78 contigs), ALE 64.5→52.13 Mb (239→72 contigs).

k-mer / heterozygosity

FastK (k=21) → hetmers (-L explicit cutoff after the tool's default arg proved broken) → peak_agregation. Smudgeplot's own plotting frontend (v0.4.0dev) had four internal C++/R version-inconsistency bugs; bypassed by classifying the raw coverage-pair output directly. Result for both strains: minor-allele-frequency distribution peaks cleanly at 0.50 (AB shape), no secondary AAB peak — genuine heterozygosity, not masked duplication.

Synteny

MUMmer4 nucmer --maxmatch -c 100, delta-filter -i 90 -l 1000, show-coords -rclT on the corrected purged assemblies. Self-alignment (within-genome duplication blocks: 10,248 HS2 / 10,291 ALE) combined with cross-alignment (184 HS2↔ALE blocks) into a single figure with duplication overlaid as shaded bands.

Telomere QC

tidk explore --minimum 5 --maximum 12 for de novo repeat-unit discovery (top hit AAACCCT, a rotation of the canonical plant/green-algal TTTAGGG telomere motif), then per-contig end classification. Variants within 20kb of a non-telomere-confirmed contig end are flagged as reduced-confidence; none of the headline candidates in §3 fall in a flagged region.

Variant calling

bcftools mpileup/call (diploid, default ploidy) as primary caller. GATK HaplotypeCaller run independently on identical alignments as cross-validation — native AVX PairHMM for HS2; for ALE, the native path segfaulted deterministically at one locus (confirmed via kernel crash logs as a native-library issue, not a data problem), worked around with the pure-Java LOGLESS_CACHING implementation (same algorithm, no numerical difference) via an 8-way genome-scattered parallelization. The entire procedure repeated reciprocally — both strains' reads mapped onto the ALE assembly instead of HS2 — as an independent, coordinate-system-agnostic check. Structural variants: pbsv 2.11.0 and Sniffles2 2.8.0, run independently and cross-checked against each other.

Short-read cross-validation

Illumina short-read data from three independent collection dates (Apr 2023, Nov 2023, Oct 2024; HS2 independently resequenced each date) mapped with bwa mem onto the corrected reference. Allele-frequency support queried at every candidate site per timepoint, giving a temporal-emergence signature in addition to simple presence/absence.

Annotation

Trinity transcriptome re-mapped onto the corrected assembly with GMAP. Gene calls quality-gated (≥90% coverage, ≥90% identity, ≤50kb span — excludes chimeric GMAP alignments, 142/78,759 raw alignments failed this) and matched to existing Trinity/Trinotate UniProt/GO/KEGG annotation at the transcript-locus level (isoform-suffix-agnostic), since functional search was not run exhaustively per isoform.

Cross-strain comparison

HS19 (NaOCl-selected) and HMF (5-HMF-selected, 2 timepoints) short reads mapped onto the identical corrected reference and called with bcftools against timepoint-matched HS2 baselines. Compared to ALE's candidate list both by exact position and by gene symbol — see §6 for the asymmetry this comparison carries and how it's handled.

07

Response to expert review

An expert reviewer raised six methodological concerns on an earlier version of this analysis. All six are now fully resolved.

1Reported heterozygosity (0.0036%) is inconsistent with an apparent two-peak k-mer spectrum; the second peak may reflect duplication or repeat content rather than true heterozygosity. Recommended Smudgeplot and self-synteny analysis.

Response

Confirmed founded, and now directly measured. Self-synteny blocks at 100.0% identity, elevated pre-purge BUSCO duplication (14.9%/10.1%, collapsing to 0.5%/1.2% post-correction), and purge_dups flagging 23%/19% of each raw assembly as duplicate content together explained the original inconsistency. Smudgeplot, the direct purpose-built test, independently confirms a genuine AB heterozygosity signal in both strains with no secondary AAB duplication peak — heterozygosity and duplication are two real, coexisting properties of this genome, not one masking the other.

Status: resolved
2HS2 (66.6 Mb) and ALE (64.5 Mb) assembly sizes differ by ~2.1 Mb — real deletion, or an assembly-processing artifact?

Response

Traced to the root cause: purge_dups had been applied to HS2 only, and with miscalibrated automatic cutoffs. Rerun consistently on both assemblies with coverage-anchored manual cutoffs (§4). Once purged identically, the gap shrinks from 2.1 Mb to 0.87 Mb and reverses direction — the original difference was predominantly a processing artifact, not a real ALE-lineage deletion.

Status: resolved
3T2T completion isn't required for this comparison, but caution is warranted for SNPs/SVs near contig ends.

Response

Agreed. Per-contig telomere classification already existed (tidk-based); now explicitly propagated as a confidence annotation on every reported variant (§4).

Status: resolved — 35/406 variants (8.6%) flagged; 0/6 candidate genes affected.
4If ALE is a direct HS2-derived mutant, structural differences should be minimal — given the duplication signal, the synteny figure should show duplicated regions as boxes, which it currently does not.

Response

Correctly identified a gap between two analyses run separately but never combined: the existing figure showed only cross-genome synteny restricted to uniquely-matching contigs, which by construction excludes the duplicated/multi-mapping content that would appear as boxes.

Status: resolved Figure rebuilt on the corrected assemblies, combining the cross-genome synteny backbone (184 blocks) with within-genome duplicated-block coordinates (10,248 HS2 / 10,291 ALE) overlaid as shaded bands.
5In a duplicated genome, "1:1" orthology/synteny assignments risk misassigning paralogs.

Response

Agreed — a material risk given the confirmed duplication content. Cross-referenced every candidate against the self-synteny duplicated-block coordinates, and extended this into an explicit, unconditional pass/fail criterion applied genome-wide (§5), not a spot-check on a handful of pre-selected genes.

Status: resolved "Clear of duplication" is one of five criteria applied systematically to all ~4,146 genome-wide candidate sites.
6Requested the k-mer analysis, Smudgeplot, self-synteny analysis, and exact workflow/options for closer review.

Response

The complete pipeline is now documented command-by-command in §4 above, including every non-default parameter and the reasoning behind it.

Status: resolved
7Functional annotation completeness, and cross-check of a previously reported ABC-transporter structural variant.

Response

Two self-audit findings from this pass. First, the transcript-level functional annotation table (57,471 transcripts) was found to have 0% of its KEGG and Gene Ontology fields populated — only the BLASTX best-hit gene symbol and UniProt accession had been carried through a prior step, not the pathway/GO data nominally in those columns. This was corrected by batch-querying the UniProt REST API directly for all 3,845 unique accessions represented in the gene set; KEGG coverage is now 86.6% and GO coverage 88.0% of all transcripts. Second, a 2023.04 short-read vendor WGS report (BreakDancer, single caller, mapped to the earlier fragmented 2015 PacBio-only reference) reported a ~2 Mb inversion flanked by an ABC-transporter-G-family gene, with weak and asymmetric read-pair support (5 WT vs. 68 MT discordant pairs). Under the current corrected-assembly, cross-caller-validated SV pipeline, no inversion of this scale — or any SV at all — is called at the corresponding locus; a nearby ABCG1 homopolymer length-variant is correctly excluded by the repeat-artifact filter. We do not consider the original finding reproducible under current methodological standards and do not carry it forward as a candidate.

Status: resolved annotation gap fixed genome-wide; prior SV claim explicitly not replicated, not silently dropped.
08

Reading it together

The overall shape of the evidence points toward a targeted, few-locus explanation rather than wholesale genomic upheaval: the two genomes remain structurally collinear, the size difference that once looked like a deletion turns out to be a processing artifact, and a systematic, artifact-filtered, genome-wide screen — not a hand-picked shortlist — converges on a small set of candidates. EPHA is the mutation most worth leading with: independently re-discovered by an unbiased screen, with a clean temporal signature showing it arose during the passaging rather than pre-existing. CLPB3 is the strongest mechanistic case for standing-variation selection, with three-timepoint stability in HS2 and a matched temporal rise in ALE. That one originally-proposed candidate (PEL1/SLAD) did not survive this scrutiny, and is reported as retracted rather than quietly dropped, is itself part of why the surviving candidates should be trusted.

09

What's needed to close the gap

Open, in priority order

  • Phenotype data integration. Quantified tolerance data (growth curves, IC50/MIC for hydrolysate or HMF, ALE vs. HS2) — and specifically Raman/FTIR spectroscopy, intended as the direct biochemical bridge from genotype to phenotype (does ACOX4's lipid-metabolism signature show up as a measurable lipid-composition shift; does CLPB3/EPHA's stress-response signature correlate with any measurable biochemical marker) — not yet integrated. The single largest remaining gap.
  • Equivalent rigor funnel for HS19/HMF. The convergent-evolution comparison (§5) currently rests on raw, single-caller HS19/HMF variant calls; a defensible convergence claim needs the identical five-criterion funnel applied there before the gene-symbol overlap can be treated as confirmed rather than suggestive.
  • Targeted confirmation of SYGM2/GLOX. PCR fragment-length assay spanning the microsatellite, since this candidate cannot clear the unconditional repeat-artifact filter on its own despite otherwise-strong support.
  • Sanger/PCR confirmation of the sure candidates before final submission — the standard wet-lab confirmation step this computational pipeline cannot substitute for. Primer-design reference sequences (±300bp flanking, REF and reconstructed-ALT) are prepared for all 30 sure candidates, with 9 flagged for elevated PCR-slippage/mispriming risk (≥20bp homopolymer/short-repeat run within the immediate flank).
Pipeline: hifiasm 0.25.0 → corrected purge_dups → FastK/Smudgeplot → MUMmer4 → bcftools + GATK (cross-validated, both reference directions) → pbsv + Sniffles2 → GMAP (quality-gated) + UniProt BLASTX best-hit → UniProt REST batch GO/KEGG cross-reference → short-read temporal validation (3 timepoints) → HS19/HMF comparative screen. Evidence-tier language throughout (confirmed / pending / retracted) is deliberate — unmarked claims in §1–5 are directly measured and cross-validated; §9 is the explicit boundary of what's been verified so far.
